title: Proposed wind farm off Delmarva coast takes a step forward with regulators
summary: The Bureau of Ocean Energy Management issued a final environmental impact statement this week on a proposed wind farm off the Delmarva coast, moving the 80,000-acre project one step closer to reality.
content:
by Maryland Matters Staff, Maryland Matters August 1, 2024

by Maryland Matters Staff, Maryland Matters August 1, 2024

The Bureau of Ocean Energy Management issued a final environmental impact statement this week on a proposed wind farm off the Delmarva coast, moving the 80,000-acre project one step closer to reality.

The statement, which is expected to be published this week in the Federal Register, identifies a 114-turbine project that could ultimately generate up to 2,200 megawatts of electricity as the preferred alternative for the project. Plans call for the almost 940-foot-tall turbines to be situated 11 miles off the coast of Ocean City at their closest point to the shore, and be connected to power substations near Indian River in Delaware for distribution.

US Wind had originally proposed 121 turbines for the Maryland Offshore Wind Project, but scaled the project back slightly to allow an additional one-mile buffer from shipping lanes on the eastern edge of the project. US Wind CEO Jeff Grybowski welcomed the issuance of the environmental impact statement this week.

“We applaud BOEM for the comprehensive and thorough review of our federal permit application,” he said in a prepared statement. “We are now one step closer to securing all of our federal permits by the end of this year, and look forward to the day we can get steel in the water.”

US Wind said the next step, a record of decision from the bureau, is expected in September, with approval from other federal regulatory agencies expected by the end of this year. Onshore construction could begin next year, and the project could begin generating power in 2027.

It is the latest step in process that began in 2014, when US Wind secured leases for two federal off-shore parcels. The formal environmental review process began two years ago.
